payload.name: Extract explicit status assertions as state candidates
payload.description: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly states the current condition or status of an entity (person, business, project), generate a state candidate even if the statement is brief or in casual conversation.
content: During extraction: when a message explicitly states the current status or condition of an entity (e.g., doing well, struggling, open, closed, on track), create a 'state' candidate linked to that entity and the message, even if the statement is brief or embedded in casual conversation.

solves: The diagnosed failure was that a short explicit status update ('the store's doing great') produced no extraction candidate, so the fact never entered memory. The abstract mechanism is under-extraction of clear state assertions when they appear in casual or small-talk turns. This rule applies to any future message containing an explicit current-status statement about any entity, and ensures such facts are promoted to state memories regardless of brevity or conversational context. It does not apply to opinions, future intentions, or statements requiring inference.
